title: `Core\Test::assertThrows` with a class that is not `Throwable` compiles, and the assertion can never pass.
text: `Test::assertThrows(fn (): void => { }, P::class)` with a plain class `P`, and `Test::assertThrows($body, "RuntimeError")` with a string, both pass `nvs check`. Nothing can throw a `P`, so the first fails on every run with `returned without throwing P`. The second compares by the name and works, so a typo in the string is found only when the test runs. It closes when the second argument is a `class<Throwable>` and anything else is a compile error, with a conformance case.
